newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crudes firm in Asia, action returns to wet market.
newsitem.headline: Crudes firm in Asia, action returns to wet market.

text.p: Crude oil futures firmed in late Asia trade on Friday, buoyed by the rally overnight while the wet market regained some momentum after trading premiums eased, traders said.
A Japanese market participant attributed the recent rollercoaster ride in oil prices to speculative fund trading.
"The market's hardly likely to change so drastically overnight (otherwise)," he said.
January cash Brent was assessed at $23.25/23.30, up about 10 cents from late U.S. trading on Thursday.
In paper spreads, Brent/Dubai was believed done at $1.95.
January Brent/Dubai was notionally assessed at $1.95/2.00.
Brent spreads were notionally assessed at 55/60 cents for December/January, 53/58 cents for both January/February and February/March.
In the wet market, a series of Gulf crude oil deals were reported done, some of them at significantly lower premiums than deals done earlier.

Among light crude grades, two January Lower Zakum were reported exchanged at ADNOC plus 58 cents. In both cases the buyer was believed to be a major. The level of the deal was about seven cents lower than the last deal reported done.

A January Umm Shaif was believed traded between two majors at ADNOC plus 65 cents. A January Qatar Marine was confirmed done at a premium of 28 cents above the official selling price, a level some 20 cents below an earlier deal. The cargo was sold from a Japanese trading company to a major.

Traders provided mixed assessments for the premium for January Murban which was last confirmed traded at ADNOC plus 65 cents. Some traders said the premium has dropped by about 10 cents, while others argued that the premium remained firm.
January Dubai was rumoured offered at a high of 80 cents above the official selling price.--M.Yoshikawa/Tokyo
